clue.text: Cutback tough on F

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for cut from its end to its start

parts.note: to cut is to clip
something tough is hard

explanation.surface: A complaint that a spending cut has been hard on someone called F.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CLIP into PILC. Throughout this puzzle F stands for FISH, the second half of 20/11 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilchard is a small oily sea creature of the herring family, so it is one kind of F, the puzzle's shorthand for fish.

clue.text: Sound situation for F

indicators.note: Sound tells us the word for situation is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a situation is a place

explanation.surface: A sound position for someone called F.
explanation.definitionFit: The plaice is a flatfish with orange spots, an example of the puzzle's F, fish.

clue.text: See dog without a voice going round the neighbourhood

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the dog goes around the voice

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
alto is one singing voice

explanation.surface: Watching a mute dog wander around the local streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: CUR is wrapped round ALTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A short trip around the nearby area is a tour of the locality.

clue.text: F-like minx

parts.note: F is the puzzle's fish, and the huss is a fish, the dogfish sold as rock salmon
the suffix -y means like, as in sandy or silky

explanation.surface: A cheeky girl compared to someone called F.
explanation.walkthrough: HUSS is a British name for dogfish, sold in chip shops as rock salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a brazen, impudent young woman.

clue.text: Painter in front of many colours freeman towpath colours

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Painter in front of many colours freeman towpath colours': OCR has run extra words ('freeman towpath colours') into it and there is no scan; RA + IN + BOW fits the first part only.
annotationWithheld.clue: Painter in front of many colours freeman towpath colours

clue.text: F for the FT, taking in a right idiot

indicators.note: taking in means holding other letters inside

parts.note: a newspaper speaks of itself in its editorials as we
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: The paper's own fish, swallowing a proper fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT's editorial voice is 'we', so WE wraps R and ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrasse is a brightly coloured reef species, one of the puzzle's F, or fish.

clue.text: F stirring mud during dourness return of counter

indicators.note: during means the stirred letters sit inside the other piece
return of tells us to read the word for counter backwards

parts.note: a teller is someone who counts, as a bank clerk or vote counter

indicators.note: stirring means the letters of mud are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone called F stirs up mud while a counter is returned, in a gloomy mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' makes DMU from MUD; 'return of' turns TELLER into RELLET, which DMU sits inside. 'dourness' looks like OCR debris and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: The red mullet is a prized Mediterranean food species, one of the puzzle's fish.

clue.text: F came to the nose

explanation.surface: Someone called F reached the nostrils.
explanation.definitionFit: F is the puzzle's fish and the smelt is a small silvery one; something that came to the nose was sniffed, so it was perceived by odour.

clue.text: People in steel cast like fire and water

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
steel is cast into a new shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: Workers inside a steel foundry, among fire and water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges STEEL as ELETS, which MEN splits after ELE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire and water are two of the four classical substances, earth and air being the others.

clue.text: I act less fitting a heroine of Greek tragedy

indicators.note: fitting is read as fitting together, assembling these letters in a new order

explanation.surface: An actor doing less in a role suitable for a tragic heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Euripides wrote a play about the queen who died in her husband's place and was brought back from Hades by Heracles.

clue.text: Stick to this period and this situation

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the present era
here is this place

explanation.surface: An instruction to hold fast to the present time and place.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick is to cling or bond firmly to something.

clue.text: See 20
F, a king with a merry conclusion

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme

indicators.note: conclusion of merry points to its final letter

explanation.surface: A fish linked with a cheerful monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme king is 'a merry old soul', which ties the surface together.
explanation.definitionFit: Coley is a cheap white food species related to cod, an example of the puzzle's fish.

clue.text: Butter melted without intelligence but with energy should burn well

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the melted letters go round the intelligence
melted butter loses its shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: IQ is the measure of intelligence
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Melted butter, with no brains but plenty of energy, ought to make a good fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melted' rearranges BUTTER and 'without' puts it outside IQ: BR + IQ + UETT, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: A block of compressed coal dust or charcoal is made as fuel for a fire.

clue.text: Acknowledge success of dog

parts.note: to bow is to acknowledge applause
a wow is a great hit

explanation.surface: Taking a bow for a dog's triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Children call a dog by the sound of its bark.

clue.text: Strike to be raised during delay with F

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Strike to be raised during delay with F': WAIT round HIT gives W-HIT-AIT but no clue word gives the EBA (ABE backwards) needed, so the clue looks misread and there is no scan.

clue.text: Prince with one qualification to be F

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
I is the Roman numeral one
a but is a reservation or qualification

explanation.surface: A prince with a single reservation about becoming a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a very large flatfish, an example of the puzzle's F, fish.

clue.text: F, apart from copper a among would-be actors

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one

indicators.note: among means the copper sits inside the drama school

parts.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London, where actors train
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A fish, except for a policeman among drama students.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is London's best-known drama school. The 'a' after copper does nothing; it may be an OCR slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The barracuda is a fierce tropical predator with long teeth, one of the puzzle's fish.

clue.text: "Kill your speed" increaser

explanation.surface: Advice to slow down, framed as a murder.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill by squeezing the neck is to strangle; the pedal or lever feeding fuel to an engine makes the vehicle go faster.

clue.text: F is what goes on the bride's finger

parts.note: her refers to the bride, a woman
what goes on the finger at a wedding is a ring

explanation.surface: A fish described as the band slipped on at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'her ring' is what goes on the bride's finger.
explanation.definitionFit: The herring is a silvery North Atlantic food species, one of the puzzle's fish.

clue.text: Bowlers, as it were, or the basic F

explanation.surface: Cricketers, so to speak, or the simplest pet.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowlers here are things kept in bowls, not cricket players.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange carp are the classic pet kept in a glass bowl, and they are the most ordinary kind of fish a child owns.

clue.text: American measures student tries out

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

indicators.note: out means the letters of tries are disordered

explanation.surface: A pupil makes attempts at American quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: US spelling of the metric volume unit, a thousand cubic centimetres.

clue.text: Bowler, as it were, for F car with shell

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Bowler, as it were, for F car with shell': a lob-bowler plus a shelled fish fits, but 'car' has no job and the clue looks misread; no scan.
annotationWithheld.clue: Bowler, as it were, for F car with shell

clue.text: Fs put on for speed

explanation.surface: Fish that someone wears to go fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays of a flat kind are a group of fish; boots with blades or wheels are worn to glide quickly.

clue.text: Lunch to be prepared when receiving sickness benefit

indicators.note: a lunch prepared is made up, so these letters are made up anew

explanation.surface: A meal is made while someone is off work sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges LUNCH TO BE. The phrase is old British slang for being paid by a sick club.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for drawing payments from a workers' sick fund.

clue.text: Time to heavily defeat F

parts.note: to rout is to beat soundly

explanation.surface: Time to give a fish a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a freshwater game species, one of the puzzle's fish.

clue.text: F after loan?

explanation.surface: A fish that follows a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: F is the puzzle's fish and this predator is one; a moneylender charging extortionate interest gets the same name after the word loan.

clue.text: F is right in a row

indicators.note: in means right is placed inside the row

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A fish is right in the middle of a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a tiny herring-like species, one of the puzzle's fish.

clue.text: Valiant man or horse

explanation.surface: A brave fellow or a steed.
explanation.definitionFit: One who works or fights like a hero from Troy is a stout fellow; the wooden steed full of Greek soldiers was the city's undoing.

clue.text: Begin holding dollars (American) to foster romantic illusions

indicators.note: holding means the first word wraps around the others

parts.note: to begin is to start
D is an abbreviation for dollars

explanation.surface: Starting out with American money to nurture fantasies of love.
explanation.walkthrough: START holds D and US after its STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The glittering stuff of dreams is the dreamy, starry-eyed glamour people imagine in love and fame.

clue.text: Property such as houses or car

explanation.surface: A piece of property, perhaps houses or a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A landed property or a housing development is an estate, and a long car with a rear door and cargo space is an estate car in Britain.

clue.text: Cutters are distressed by maxims

parts.note: to fret is to be worried or upset
saws are old sayings

explanation.surface: Cutting tools are upset by proverbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine-bladed tools for cutting curved patterns in wood are a kind of cutter.
